scope.description: Check contributor eligibility at the verification aggregation boundary. Establish a fixed configuration containing three voters, including the local leader, and at least one nonvoter. Register a verification through Raft.verifyLeader and deliver an affirmative notification from the nonvoter's actual replication object while withholding all remote voter contributions. Observe whether verification reaches its successful quorum branch. Independently identify contributors by configured ServerID and Suffrage.
assumptions: The local node is a voter and is executing one leader generation.
Membership, peer identities, and replication objects remain unchanged throughout the check.
Each delivered affirmative contribution is correlated with its originating replication object.
Remote voter notifications and unrelated replication notifications are withheld until the stopping observation.
An affirmative nonvoter notification is an explicit boundary input; its generation through a complete distributed execution is not assumed established.
excluded: Legal distributed history establishing an obsolete leader and producing the selected responses
Stale FSM reads or other client-visible consequences
Request freshness and responses to exchanges initiated before verification registration
Membership changes, replication-object replacement, and cross-generation contributions
Transport correlation and production deployment exposure

properties.reason: Actual result fields are compared after independent prerequisite association

adaptations: Manually initialize fixed membership and one leader generation using actual Raft fields and setupLeaderState; omit election, persistent startup, no-op dispatch, transport, and replication workers.
Instantiate followerReplication objects using the fields and membership inclusion shown in startStopReplication; do not execute its asynchronous worker startup.
Call Raft.verifyLeader under exclusive ownership before starting leaderLoop instead of dispatching through public VerifyLeader.
Inject one affirmative notification through the selected actual followerReplication.notifyAll boundary.
Queue a separate initialized terminal future as a processing marker. Its manufactured tally controls stopping only and is never evidence of primary verification support.
Use a one-hour lease timeout to keep the lease outside the short experiment. Timeout or changed leader state prevents result emission.
Read primary completion from its actual error channel after joining leaderLoop; pending means no success by this controlled endpoint, not eventual noncompletion.
blockers: Open review issue 33dab19bc1db4bb197e4ddee7f25afd2 [api.go:800:1000,api.go:500:640,raft.go:455:666,raft.go:667:826,raft.go:827:1100,replication.go:1:202,future.go:1:314,commitment.go:1:104]: The saved assertion compares success for equality with input.expected_success for both operations. For verify-V1, expected_success is true, so unsuccessful or pending completion would be attributed to check_verify_voter_support even though no nonvoter supplied a contribution.; The observable property's description explicitly states that failure of the permitted control alone does not establish nonvoter substitution; the executable equality does not preserve that distinction.

Stale FSM reads or other client-visible consequences

Distributed response reachability, request freshness, membership changes, generation transitions, transport correlation, and stale-read consequences remain unresolved.
The primary can remain pending at the completed boundary endpoint; this establishes only absence of success through that endpoint.
Marker failure, timeout, missing registration, changed leader state, or failed goroutine join produces no property result.
Internal completion is measured directly; public VerifyLeader dispatch and client observation are not exercised.
The encoding issue does not negate the observed verify-N mismatch: that witness violates the intended one-way eligibility condition as well as the current equality.

The API's voter-eligibility expectation remains an explicit inference from combined responsibilities. The separate connectivity lease is not a prerequisite checked by verification completion and does not establish an alternative voter-backed verification mechanism here.

The fixture bypasses NewRaft validation, elections, runLeader's no-op dispatch, transport, and replication worker startup. Its result establishes an internal aggregation-boundary behavior, not a legal distributed history or public-call reproduction.
Request freshness, membership transitions, generation changes, stale leadership, stale reads, and production exposure remain unresolved. Eligibility alone would not exclude those other bad outcomes.
Go test PASS reports successful harness execution; the emitted nonvoter observations contain the property mismatch.
The available revision schema cannot express a direct-check predicate replacement. A controller-supported checker encoding revision and actual recheck are required; no graph F2 change is proposed.
